OBGYN Disparities in the US

Katherine Zeng

2025-03-23

Load and clean the dataset

tuesdata <- tidytuesdayR::tt_load(2025, week = 8)
## ---- Compiling #TidyTuesday Information for 2025-02-25 ----
## --- There are 2 files available ---
## 
## 
## ── Downloading files ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## 
##   1 of 2: "article_dat.csv"
##   2 of 2: "model_dat.csv"
article_dat <- tuesdata$article_dat
model_dat <- tuesdata$model_dat

Data Wrangling

# create column of durations 
time_dat <- article_dat %>% mutate(duration = study_year_end - study_year_start) %>% 
  filter(study_year_end != -99 & study_year_start != 99) %>% 
  mutate(study_type = tolower(study_type))

# create df of only study focus areas
topic_dat <- article_dat %>% select(access_to_care:covid) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "topic", values_to = "value") %>% 
  group_by(topic) %>% 
  summarise(total = sum(value, na.rm = T)) %>% 
  arrange(desc(total))

Article Analysis

Initial Exploration

Notes: * retrospective cohorts are the most popular study type by far * top study topics areas: * health outcomes * treatment received * access to care * maternal morbidity and mortality * uterine cancer

# stacked histogram of studies by study type
ggplot(time_dat, aes(x = duration, fill = study_type, groups = study_type)) +
  xlim(0, 45) +
  geom_histogram(na.rm = T) 
## `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value with `binwidth`.

# simple bar chart of topics addressed
ggplot(topic_dat, aes(x = reorder(topic, -total), y = total)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  ylim(0, 200) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45))
## Warning: Removed 1 row containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_bar()`).

# exploratory violin plot
time_dat %>% ggplot(aes(x = study_type, y = duration, fill = study_type)) +
  geom_violin(outlier.colour = "transparent", width = 1) +
  geom_boxplot(color = "grey", alpha = 0.2, width = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_viridis(discrete = T, name = "") +
  theme_ipsum() +
  xlab("") +
  ylab("Study Duration (Years)") +
  ylim(0, 25) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())

keyword analysis

# guide from r-graph-gallery.com

# create 3 columns needed for the plot
keywords <- article_dat %>% separate_rows(keywords, sep = "; ") %>% 
  separate_rows(keywords, sep = ", ") %>% 
  mutate(keywords = tolower(keywords)) %>% 
  group_by(year, keywords) %>% 
  summarise(count = n())
## `summarise()` has grouped output by 'year'. You can override using the
## `.groups` argument.
# simple raw graph - many different words every year!
streamgraph(keywords, key = "keywords", value = "count", date = "year", height = "300px", width = "1000px", offset = "expand") %>% 
  sg_fill_brewer("PuOr")
## Warning in widget_html(name, package, id = x$id, style = css(width =
## validateCssUnit(sizeInfo$width), : streamgraph_html returned an object of class
## `list` instead of a `shiny.tag`.
## Warning: `bindFillRole()` only works on htmltools::tag() objects (e.g., div(),
## p(), etc.), not objects of type 'list'.
# narrow it down by top 50 of each year
keywords %>% group_by(year) %>% 
  arrange(desc(count), .by_group = T) %>% 
  top_n(50) %>% streamgraph(key = "keywords", value = "count", date = "year", height = "300px", width = "1000px", interpolate = "linear", offset = "expand") %>% 
  sg_fill_brewer("PuOr")

keywords continued - factored by other variables

# breakdown of keywords by journal
journal_facet <- article_dat %>% separate_rows(keywords, sep = "; ") %>% 
  separate_rows(keywords, sep = ", ") %>% 
  mutate(keywords = tolower(keywords)) %>% 
  group_by(year, journal, keywords) %>% 
  summarise(count = n())
## `summarise()` has grouped output by 'year', 'journal'. You can override using
## the `.groups` argument.
journal_facet
## # A tibble: 3,612 × 4
## # Groups:   year, journal [60]
##     year journal                                       keywords            count
##    <dbl> <chr>                                         <chr>               <int>
##  1  2010 American journal of obstetrics and gynecology african americans       1
##  2  2010 American journal of obstetrics and gynecology aged                    1
##  3  2010 American journal of obstetrics and gynecology european continent…     1
##  4  2010 American journal of obstetrics and gynecology female                  1
##  5  2010 American journal of obstetrics and gynecology genetic associatio…     1
##  6  2010 American journal of obstetrics and gynecology haplotypes              1
##  7  2010 American journal of obstetrics and gynecology humans                  1
##  8  2010 American journal of obstetrics and gynecology laminin                 1
##  9  2010 American journal of obstetrics and gynecology linkage disequilib…     1
## 10  2010 American journal of obstetrics and gynecology middle aged             1
## # ℹ 3,602 more rows
for (j in unique(journal_facet$journal)) {
  img <- journal_facet %>% filter("journal" == j) %>% 
    group_by(year) %>% 
    arrange(desc(count), .by_group = T) %>% 
    top_n(10) %>% streamgraph(key = "keywords", value = "count", date = "year", height = "300px", width = "1000px", offset = "zero") %>% 
    sg_fill_brewer("PuOr")
}
